summary: Static technical audit against the expanded file (scripts/expand-md.js confirmed a no-op here — zero {{prompt:}} markers, zero fenced Prompt blocks) plus four compendiums (platform_and_boundaries, research_claims, prompts, pedagogy technical subset). This supplementary is a pure-prose theory reading page (backpressure / chain-compounding / session-reach / the governor question) with no platform-capability claims, no [Skill:] references, and exactly one citation: a verbatim quote from Lucas F. da Costa's personal blog, correctly labeled [practitioner direct] with a valid freshness stamp in the maintainer's Source-verification block. Independently re-fetched https://www.lucasfcosta.com/blog/backpressure-is-all-you-need (2026-07-12 WebFetch) -- URL alive (200), byline and date match (Lucas Fernandes da Costa, 2026-05-23), and the quoted sentence appears verbatim (only the source's own lead-in "My maxim:" is trimmed, not altered). The one numeric figure in the body -- "if one step were 85 percent reliable, ten unverified steps would land near 20" -- is explicitly subjunctive and labeled in-body "an illustration, not a measurement," with the maintainer block independently reinforcing the zombie-stat guard ("Do NOT let edits promote it to a measured constant"); despite the coincidental round number, this is not the same shape as a cited AI-failure-rate zombie stat and does not need a source-type label since no empirical claim is being made. Given the file's narrow scope (no prompts, no platform claims, no skills, one already-well-hedged citation), the overwhelming majority of the platform_and_boundaries and prompts compendium rules are N/A by subject-matter mismatch, not by omission -- each carries a one-line reason. No blocking findings.
